findings.reason: the rubric requires §2 to name why the existing `label_axes` mechanism cannot be extended, and the plan gives only a behavioural reason, not that comparison.
findings.text: §2 leaves `_render_timeseries_mpl` unchanged and clears the x-label after drawing in `time_trace_figure_mpl` (`figures.py:102`), but the renderer already owns panel-label suppression through `label_axes` (mpl.py:554-580), which the builder already drives at `figures.py:98`; the plan does not state why that parameter cannot be split into x/y control instead of bypassing it

findings.reason: the plan's stated goal is "a stacked trace figure's time axis once", so it must either extend the alt stacked figure or state explicitly that the alt backend is out of scope.
findings.text: the altair trace figure stacks per-trace charts (`render_alt(ts)` mapped over traces, combined by `alt.vconcat`) and each chart hard-codes `x=alt.X("time:Q", title="Time [s]")` at `alt.py:393`, so the alt backend repeats the time-axis title per panel and §2 removes it only for matplotlib; the census of stacked-trace composition sites is `figures.py:89` (fixed) and `mcp.py:294-299` (untouched)

duplicate_owner-1.reason: the altair stack in server/mcp.py belongs to the served MCP application, not the matplotlib figures this plan serves; plan v1 §2 narrows its title and text to the matplotlib stack and records the server stack as left unchanged

thin_wrapper-1.reason: plan v1 §2 extends the renderer's label suppression with a private label_time keyword that alone controls the time x-label, driven by time_trace_figure_mpl for every panel but the bottom

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_ink/_decimate.py` hides equal-count binning and extreme preservation behind one private function shared by both backends, and §2 adds two lines to the builder rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `_render_timeseries_alt` (`imas_ink/alt.py:370`) and the altair stacking in `imas_ink/server/mcp.py:294-299` are a second owner of the repeated time-axis label that §2 fixes only for matplotlib.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 states `trace_max_points` "retires nothing, because no style field bounds a trace's resolution today" and §2 states "It adds no public name".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §1 names both and only both TimeSeries renderers (`imas_ink/mpl.py:549`, `imas_ink/alt.py:370`) as the decimation sites, and a search of `imas_ink/` and `tests/` finds no decimation/downsample/envelope/point-limit machinery (only PyVista mesh `n_points` under `three_d/`), so the plan rebuilds nothing that exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 clears the x-label post-hoc in `time_trace_figure_mpl` instead of extending the existing `label_axes` mechanism that already owns panel-label suppression, and does not say why it cannot be extended.
